mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES rebounds from a sharp one-week drop, commuting and nearby errand trips recover with a short lag, lifting RETAIL_REC within four weeks. In this snapshot, the abrupt fall in WORKPLACES at t-1w followed by partial recovery at t-0w should translate into higher retail visitation if office attendance stabilizes.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell from -8.6 at t-2w to -32.6 at t-1w and then recovered to -6.4 at t-0w
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES remains near or below the current level while RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not rise above the prior 28-day mean, the mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A recent jump in GROCERY_PHARM reflects precautionary stock-up behavior that substitutes away from discretionary shopping and suppresses RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks. If the grocery spike fades, the retail drag should weaken quickly; if it persists, retail stays depressed.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises above 30 points and stays elevated for at least 2 consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM reached 34.6 at t-1w after 27.4 and 29.0 in prior weeks
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM stays above 30 yet RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days does not fall below the prior 14-day mean, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: The combination of weaker TRANSIT and weaker WORKPLACES signals reduced circulation through city centers, which lowers spontaneous retail visits over the next four weeks. This mechanism is strongest when both commuting proxies remain below baseline together rather than moving in opposite directions.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT stayed negative across all four weeks and WORKPLACES was negative in every week
failure_condition: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES stay below baseline but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days exceeds the prior 28-day mean, the joint-circulation mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A renewed rise in RESIDENTIAL mobility indicates more time spent near home, which shifts consumption toward local necessities and away from discretionary retail outlets. Over the next week, that home-centered behavior should keep RETAIL_REC from improving unless RESIDENTIAL falls back quickly.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL was 10.9 at t-1w and 6.7 at t-0w
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL rises above 10 but RETAIL_REC improves over the next 7 days relative to the prior 7 days, the home-substitution claim fails.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS mobility rises, discretionary outdoor activity competes with indoor retail trips and depresses RETAIL_REC after a short lag. The recent park surge at t-1w should matter only if it persists, because a one-week spike that immediately reverses will not sustain retail weakness.
candidate_trigger: PARKS increases by at least 5 points from the prior week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS moved from -14.9 at t-2w to -4.6 at t-1w before returning to -16.9 at t-0w
failure_condition: If PARKS rises by at least 5 points yet RETAIL_REC does not fall below its prior 14-day mean within 14 days, the substitution effect is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Retail recovers only when TRANSIT and WORKPLACES improve together, because the joint return of commuting and office attendance restores passing foot traffic to shopping areas. If one rebounds while the other remains weak, the retail effect will be muted or absent over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both remain below baseline in the snapshot
failure_condition: If both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES improve from the current snapshot but RETAIL_REC still does not rise relative to the last 28 days, the interaction mechanism fails.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in TRANSIT below the current level signals a renewed constraint on mobility and suppresses retail visits within two weeks. The effect should appear when transit weakens further, because fewer station trips reduce incidental shopping opportunities.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -15 points for 2 consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT was -15.1 at t-1w and -10.6 at t-0w
failure_condition: If TRANSIT falls below -15 for two weeks but RETAIL_REC does not decline versus the prior 14-day mean, the constraint signal is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent combination of high GROCERY_PHARM and elevated RESIDENTIAL means households are consolidating trips and staying local, which reduces discretionary shopping over the next four weeks. This mechanism fails if grocery activity normalizes while residential time at home stays high, because then the retail drag should weaken.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM stayed above 27 in all four weeks and RESIDENTIAL stayed above baseline in all four weeks
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM remains elevated and RESIDENTIAL remains above baseline but RETAIL_REC rises above its prior 28-day mean over the next 28 days, the trip-consolidation hypothesis fails.
